chain.label: Misaligned panels during manufacture led to misdrilled lower rivet row of the S-4L lap joint
chain.trigger: during drilling of the S-4L lap joint, the crown skin panel and the upper left fuselage panel were misaligned, so most of the lower rivet row holes were misdrilled

chain.label: Boeing quality assurance did not identify the poor lap joint workmanship; accident crown panel lacked an inspection stamp
chain.trigger: the investigation could not determine why the crown skin panel was replaced or how the poor repair was not identified in the QA process

chain.label: Ovalized/double-drilled, offset holes with rivets not filling them, significantly reducing panel fatigue life
chain.trigger: Many of the installed rivets did not completely fill the holes in the lower skin panel, which significantly reduced the fatigue life of the panel

caused_by.evidence: hole quality... was not in accordance with Boeing specifications or standard manufacturing practices and showed a lack of attention to detail and extremely poor manufacturing technique
The Boeing QA process for an in-factory re-work followed the same steps as factory production, requiring multiple inspections and approvals

chain.label: Fatigue cracking initiated at rivet hole 85 near entry into service and grew as multiple site damage with each pressurization cycle
chain.trigger: The pressurization loads on the fuselage skin initiated fatigue cracking at rivet hole 85 almost immediately after manufacture. Fatigue cracking subsequently initiated in adjacent rivets... and grew over time

caused_by.evidence: the fatigue cracking at rivet hole 85 began approximately when the airplane entered service

chain.label: Cracks linked up to critical length; residual strength insufficient and the skin section fractured and flapped open
chain.trigger: the cumulative amount of fatigue cracking reached a critical length, and the panel's residual strength was not sufficient to carry the loads, which resulted in the hole flapping open

caused_by.evidence: small individual fatigue cracks grow slowly over time to a point where they link up, causing failure

chain.label: Rapid cabin decompression while climbing through FL340
chain.trigger: experienced a rapid decompression while climbing through flight level 340

caused_by.evidence: resulted in the hole flapping open and rapid depressurization of the airplane

chain.label: FAA guidance on time of useful consciousness misleading and not representative of actual performance after rapid decompression
chain.trigger: the information provided in AC 61-107A is misleading and needs to be revised to emphasize that time is of the essence in a depressurization

chain.label: Flight attendant A attempted an interphone call or P/A announcement before donning oxygen, contrary to training
chain.trigger: His decision to make the call or P/A announcement before obtaining oxygen was inconsistent with Southwest Airlines training materials

caused_by.evidence: After the decompression, flight attendant A stated that there were two 'high priority' tasks
lost consciousness, likely due to an incorrect assessment of his time of useful consciousness

chain.label: Flight attendant A and an off-duty employee passenger assisting him lost consciousness from hypoxia
chain.trigger: he lost consciousness, fell, and struck his nose on the forward partition; the employee passenger lost consciousness and fell while attempting to assist

caused_by.evidence: flight attendant A attempted to perform actions before obtaining oxygen and lost consciousness
If pressure is lost, prompt action is required to maintain occupant consciousness

chain.label: Minor injuries: fractured/lacerated nose to flight attendant A and laceration to the employee passenger
chain.trigger: one crewmember and one nonrevenue off-duty airline employee passenger sustained minor injuries

caused_by.evidence: struck the forward partition, and sustained a laceration and fracture of his nose... He sustained a laceration above his eye during the fall

chain.label: Emergency descent and diversion to Yuma International Airport, landed without further incident
chain.trigger: The flight crew conducted an emergency descent and diverted to Yuma International Airport (NYL)... The airplane landed about 1629 on runway 21R at NYL without further incident.

caused_by.evidence: the captain declared an emergency with air traffic control and requested a lower altitude
